html:
The global security landscape is increasingly defined by heightened tensions between the United States and Iran, as military strikes and rhetoric escalate across the Middle East. Trump has threatened to target Iran’s infrastructure, including bridges and power plants, for any attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran warns of an "eye for an eye" response, vowing to stop Gulf oil flow and target regional infrastructure if the US acts on these threats.

Middle East Conflict: Reports indicate ongoing military exchanges, with Iran's Army and Revolutionary Guard claiming drone strikes on US bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait, inflicting damage and reportedly causing casualties. Satellite imagery reportedly reveals damage to US bases in Erbil and Jordan. Jordan's army intercepted four Iranian missiles and four drones, while Kuwait also reported intercepting missile and drone attacks. Separately, Iranian media reported a US strike on the island of Larak in Hormuz. Amidst these developments, a Dubai firm has finalized a deal to build new port terminals on the UAE's eastern coast, aimed at bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

US Policy & War Funding: The House of Representatives passed a $1.15 trillion defense policy bill, though Democrats largely opposed it due to the ongoing war with Iran and Donald Trump’s voter agenda. House Republicans are also preparing a separate $95 billion bill to fund the Iran war and provide aid to farmers. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has estimated the war with Iran has already cost $37.5 billion, as Trump seeks additional billions from Congress and considers military options in Mali. The US is also investigating whether Russia assisted Iran in drone attacks on CIA facilities in the Gulf.

US-Saudi Nuclear Deal: In a significant development, the US and Saudi Arabia signed a landmark nuclear cooperation agreement. The deal, approved by Trump, could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium for civilian use and is expected to give US firms "great access" to the Saudi nuclear energy program. US energy secretary Chris Wright stated the agreements uphold "the highest standards of nuclear safety and nonproliferation."

Ukraine War & Russia: Ukraine has a new military commander, Mykhailo Drapatyi, appointed after a week of nationwide protests over military strategy. Drapatyi has pledged to escalate retaliation against Russia. Meanwhile, Russia is reportedly recruiting foreign nationals from the world's poorest countries to fight in Ukraine. Prospects for peace remain dim, despite a scheduled meeting between Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and his US counterpart Marco Rubio.

Global Economy & Trade: Tesla reported lower-than-expected profits despite growing revenue, with its shares falling as the company pivots to robotics and AI, while Elon Musk's SpaceX takes a more prominent role. In media, Paramount Skydance’s £80 billion takeover of Warner Brothers moved closer to completion following conditional approval from the European Union. Globally, India is investing billions to build its domestic semiconductor industry, aiming to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.

Other Major Developments: Daniel Siad, a modeling scout linked to Jeffrey Epstein, was found dead in Paris; he had previously denied knowledge of Epstein's threats. In Australia, China's foreign ministry reacted to comments by Penny Wong, urging "relevant countries" to "stop stirring up tension." France recorded over 5,700 excess deaths during a historic heatwave in June, and a protest movement known as the "Cockroaches" is challenging India's establishment. The UK has unveiled the Brontanax fighter drone, marking a significant step into collaborative combat aircraft.
